t: Indonesia invaded on 7 December 1975, nine days after Fretilin's declaration of independence; the occupation that followed caused at least 102,800 conflict-related deaths between 1974 and 1999, by one estimate as many as 200,000.

A UN-supervised referendum in August 1999 voted clearly for independence, met by a punitive campaign of violence by pro-integration militias backed by elements of the Indonesian military, before UNTAET took over the territory on 25 October 1999.

Timor-Leste became independent on 20 May 2002; its Petroleum Fund, set up in 2005, received $23 billion from oil sales by 2021 and funds 80% of government spending, but is at risk of exhaustion as the Bayu-Undan field runs out.
dyk: Timor-Leste's name means 'East East': Timor comes from timur, 'east' in Indonesian or Malay, and Leste is 'east' in Portuguese. In Tetun the country is Timór Lorosa'e, 'where the sun rises'.
ev: On 28 November Fretilin unilaterally declares independence; nine days later, on 7 December, the Indonesian military invades East Timor.
The Indonesian military massacres more than 200 demonstrators, a turning point that brings international pressure on Indonesia.
A UN-supervised referendum votes clearly for independence; pro-integration militias backed by the Indonesian military answer with a campaign of violence, and INTERFET lands to restore order.
On 20 May the Constitution comes into force and Timor-Leste is recognised as independent by the UN, with Xanana Gusmão as its first president; it joins the UN on 27 September.
The Timor-Leste Petroleum Fund is established to turn oil and gas revenue into lasting wealth.
A crisis of unrest and factional fighting drives 155,000 people from their homes; UN security forces return to restore order.
Timor-Leste and Australia settle their maritime boundary by treaty after conciliation before the Permanent Court of Arbitration.
ASEAN announces that Timor-Leste will be admitted as its 11th full member at the October summit in Kuala Lumpur.

f.founder: Xanana Gusmão, first president, and the Constituent Assembly that approved the Constitution on 22 March 2002
f.predecessor: Portuguese Timor (1769–1975); Indonesian occupation as the province of Timor Timur (1975–1999); the United Nations Transitional Administration in East Timor (1999–2002)
